extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans and prospective attendees planning to go to RIOT LA 2017 (Los Angeles audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: A short event guide describing RIOT LA 2017: dates, venues, ticketing, lineup highlights, and nearby food/drink options aimed at readers deciding which shows to see and how to attend. Focused on the three-day alternative comedy festival in Downtown Los Angeles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event dates
rubrics_metrics.description: RIOT LA takes place January 19 through 22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One weekend in January; the guide frames planning around those dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venues / locations
rubrics_metrics.description: This year's festival will take place at the Microsoft Theater, the Novo, the Orpheum Theatre and the Theatre at Ace Hotel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike past years (which centered around a cluster of small venues on Main Street), this year's shows occur in both grandiose auditoriums and more intimate side rooms — factor venue size/ambience into which shows you choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket pricing and pass options
rubrics_metrics.description: Tickets to single shows at RIOT LA 2017 vary from $10 to over $100. A premium pass costs $159.50 and a VIP pass costs $349.50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premium pass guarantees a seat at three headlining shows; VIP pass guarantees a seat at seven shows. Use price ranges and pass guarantees to weigh cost vs. number/priority of shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass benefits and inclusions ('the Lot')
rubrics_metrics.description: Both premium and VIP passes include admission to 'the Lot', a carnival-like area with arcade games and food trucks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ancillary festival spaces and activities (games, food) are part of the value proposition for pass-holders and can influence whether a pass is worth it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance variety / genres
rubrics_metrics.description: The festival is described as a melting pot of stand-up, storytelling, musical comedy and 'indescribably bonkers performances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a broad mix of forms (including screenings and Q&As such as Blazing Saddles with Mel Brooks); choose shows based on preferred comedy subgenres and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lineup and headliners (star power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlining comedians include Ali Wong, Felipe Esparaza, Dr. Katz Live and a screening of Blazing Saddles with a Q&A from Mel Brooks; other appearances include Kyle Kinane, Eugene Mirman, Todd Barry, Nikki Glaser, Tig Notaro, Ron Funches, Beth Stelling, Rachel Bloom and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile names and special events (screenings/Q&As) are highlighted as must-see draws; use lineup prominence when prioritizing limited time or money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor-curated 'must-see' recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece is billed as 'Your guide to the best shows to see at the annual alternative comedy festival' and links to lists like '9 must-see comedy shows at RIOT LA 2017.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial curation (staff picks/must-see lists) is presented as a selection heuristic for attendees — consult those curated lists to identify standout shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nearby food and drink guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections and links advise 'Where to eat and drink in DTLA' and 'Where to eat and drink near L.A. Live,' plus listings for best Downtown Los Angeles bars and restaurants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendation: plan dining and pre/post-show activities by consulting the guide's nearby restaurant and bar suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value proposition compared to regular comedy clubs
rubrics_metrics.description: The page (via past-coverage snippets) notes that theater shows can be a tough sell in L.A. because 'You can see comedians for a few bucks any night of the week at UCB, NerdMelt or the Comedy Store.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this comparison to judge whether festival shows offer sufficiently unique or premium experiences (special lineups, larger venues, carnival atmosphere) to justify higher prices.
